subject: How to specify the latent model within one observation?

messages.author: ff1a5632abbf2fe9
messages.subject: How to specify the latent model within one observation?
parts:
Dear INLA experts?

My specified question is to implement the following model

E(y)= beta_1*x_1 + beta_2*x_2 + .... + beta_12*x_12

here, 'beta_1 + beta_2+ .... + beta_12' follow the 'rw1' model, which is
beta_2=beta_1+normal increment
beta_3=beta_2+normal increment
.....

All increments have the same normal distribution

Thanks,
Best

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to specify the latent model within one observation?
parts:
Something like 
f(beta,x,model ="rw1")
Should do this, assuming x_i are scalars. (The second argument gives deterministic fixed weights to each value of the random effect)

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to specify the latent model within one observation?
parts:
Hi, Dan

Thanks for your reply, but Idon't quite understand your answer.
Maybe I did not explain the question well, so I give a short simulation example

n=100 #sample size

#generate paremeters, a random walk strucrure
beta1 <- rnorm(n=1, mean = 0, sd = 1000000)
beta2 <- beta1 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = 100)
beta3 <- beta2 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = 100)
beta4 <- beta3 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = 100)
beta5 <- beta4 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = 100)
beta6 <- beta5 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = 100)
beta7 <- beta6 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = 100)
beta8 <- beta7 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = 100)
beta <- c(beta1,beta2,beta3,beta4,beta5,beta6,beta7,beta8)

#generate design matrix
X <- matrix(rnorm(n=800), ncol=8, nrow=n)

#generate data according to beta and X
y <- X%*%beta + rnorm(n)

In my application, I have some prior knowledge that beta has a random walk structure, and my goal is to estimate the beta parameter. It is a little bit different from the common case, in the sense that the latent effect are within one observation for distinct variables, while under the common circumstance the latent effect are between observations for a identical variable. I don't know how to implement corresponding code.


Thanks in advance,
Xing

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to specify the latent model within one observation?
parts:
On Thu, 2013-10-24 at 01:16 -0700, Zhao Xing wrote:
> Hi, Dan


here is an example, starting from yours.
H
***************

n=1000 #sample size

beta1 <- rnorm(n=1, mean = 0, sd = 1)
beta2 <- beta1 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = .1)
beta3 <- beta2 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = .1)
beta4 <- beta3 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = .1)
beta5 <- beta4 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = .1)
beta6 <- beta5 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = .1)
beta7 <- beta6 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = .1)
beta8 <- beta7 + rnorm(n=1,mean = 0, sd = .1)

#generate data according to beta and X
y <- X%*%beta + rnorm(n)

require(INLA)
r = inla(y ~ -1 + f(beta.idx, model="rw1", constr=FALSE),
data = list(beta.idx = 1:8, y = y),
control.predictor = list(A=X))
summary(r)
plot(beta, r$summary.random$beta.idx$mean)
abline(0,1)
